key_insight: Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP) separates understanding what a robot should do from learning how to do it. It combines pretrained visual-language understanding with simulation-based training for robot control.
problem_solved: Robot policies must connect scene and task understanding with executable movements, including when familiar concepts appear in new combinations.
method: Use a pretrained 27B-parameter vision-language model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning.
Connect the model to robot controls through a simple tool harness.
Apply supervised fine-tuning and GRPO on simple simulated tasks to teach robot movement.
impact: ZAP offers practitioners a recipe for pairing pretrained reasoning with simulation-trained control. It targets compositional generalization without relying on real-world robot training data, though the supplied abstract does not quantify performance.
visual_elements: Two-part diagram: pretraining teaches 'what'; simulation teaches 'how'.
Training pipeline: pretrained model → supervised fine-tuning → GRPO → robot policy.
Control-loop illustration: scene and instruction → model → tool harness → robot action.
Compositional-generalization schematic showing familiar objects and actions recombined into a new task.
paper_title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
paper_authors: Benjamin Pikus, Daniel Saunders, Mircea Mironenco, Salman Mohammadi, Mathew Mathew
